reason: Conversation 1 reaches the right conclusion (broken conductor at the old taped section), tells her to stop using it and not wiggle the cable, correctly says tape isn't a safe repair, and gives proportionate escalation (son or local vacuum repair shop) with sensible cable/plug replacement advice; its main flaw is stating the cable is 'almost certainly' the cause without noting fuse/switch can't be fully excluded. Conversation 2 asked efficient questions but then collapsed into a generic boilerplate safety block that references a 'cracked hob top', tells her to isolate at the consumer unit, and demands a qualified electrician — disproportionate and off-target for a Henry with a taped cable, with no diagnosis, no part guidance, and no use of her mention of the handy son. Both say stop using it, but only Conversation 1 actually helps.
